title: A Inventory for the Undertow
premise: Emrys Brightwater, once the conservatory's most celebrated young pianist, returns a decade after her mysterious withdrawal—as a janitor mopping the floors where she once performed. When the auction of her family's flooded coastal house surfaces an unopened letter from her dead brother, Emrys is forced to confront the question her family arranged itself around and never asked: what really happened the night he drowned. As she pieces together memory against evidence, she discovers her silence was chosen for her, not by her. The novel ends with Emrys performing publicly for the first time in ten years—not as the prodigy she was, but playing her brother's unfinished composition, finally saying it aloud.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is a former music librarian who spent seven years cataloguing the estates of deceased musicians before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a houseboat on the Welsh coast, where the tide dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unplayed Keys
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: introduces her double life at the conservatory—janitor by day, ghost by history. She cleans the concert hall where her portrait still hangs, avoiding eye contact with students who don't recognize her. Emotional beat: the ache of deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: Salt in the Grout
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: a routine cleaning job reveals water damage shaped like a coastline; she traces it absently and realizes she's drawing the shore beneath her childhood home. Flashback fragments of her brother Ianto teaching her to swim. Beat: memory as involuntary reflex.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: a solicitor's letter arrives—the Brightwater house, derelict since the flood, goes to auction in six weeks. Her mother calls, brisk and brittle, telling her not to come. Beat: dread disguised as obligation.

chapters.title: What the Janitor Hears
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with conservatory student Nia, who practices late and hears someone playing fragments in the empty hall after hours—but never sees anyone. Beat: mystery seeded; Emrys's secret night playing revealed obliquely.

chapters.title: Return to Tresillian Cove
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she travels home against her mother's wishes, standing outside the boarded house as auctioneers inventory it. She finds her childhood piano, warped and salt-ruined, on the porch. Beat: grief made physical.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: helping catalogue contents, she finds a locked writing box labeled with Ianto's initials that no one mentioned in ten years. The auctioneer says it wasn't in the estate file. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Mother of Few Words
chapters.summary: Mother, POV (Merrin): reveals her ferocious control of the family narrative—she has rehearsed every answer about Ianto's death for a decade. She warns Emrys away from the box. Beat: love expressed as censorship.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: dinner with Merrin, where both women circle the unasked question. Emrys almost mentions the box three times; each time Merrin redirects. Beat: the family art of avoidance rendered in dialogue.

chapters.title: Nia's Audition
chapters.summary: Nia, POV: preparing for the conservatory's composition prize, she asks the janitor's opinion on phrasing, unaware of who she's asking. Emrys gives advice too precise to be accidental. Beat: identity straining against disguise.

chapters.title: The Locked Box Opens
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she takes the box to a locksmith, claiming she lost the key. Inside: Ianto's notebook, an unfinished manuscript titled 'Undertow,' and a letter addressed to Emrys, sealed. Beat: the past acquires a voice.

chapters.title: Unopened
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she cannot bring herself to open the letter, carrying it for days like a stone. Interleaved: memories of Ianto composing at night while the family slept. Beat: paralysis as self-protection.

chapters.title: Father's Silence
chapters.summary: Father, POV (Aled): a retired harbormaster living alone, he remembers the night differently than Merrin allows—he was drunk, he heard something, he never said. He watches Emrys from a distance at the harbor. Beat: complicity and cowardice.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the house sells to a developer. Watching strangers measure her childhood rooms, Emrys realizes the physical past is vanishing faster than she can decode it. She bids impulsively on the ruined piano and wins. Beat: loss sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Tuning What Cannot Be Tuned
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she hires a restorer, Rhys, a gentle widower who recognizes her name but says nothing. Working on the piano becomes their shared language. Beat: tentative connection; being seen without being exposed.

chapters.title: What Nia Found
chapters.summary: Nia, POV: researching the conservatory archive for her competition essay, Nia finds clippings about Emrys Brightwater's disappearance from music—and notices the janitor's hands. Beat: suspicion kindling into recognition.

chapters.title: The Letter, Partly Read
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she steams the letter open just enough to read the first line—Ianto knew he was going to the water that night, and it wasn't an accident of wandering. She stops reading, shaking. Beat: the question taking shape.

chapters.title: Merrin's Version
chapters.summary: Merrin, POV: flashback chapter—ten years ago, Merrin found Ianto's note first and burned it, deciding the family would survive a tragedy better than a truth. Beat: antagonist reveal reframed as desperate motherhood.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Emrys and Merrin, alternating POV: on the exposed flats below the old house, Emrys asks the question directly. Merrin denies everything; Emrys shows her the notebook. Merrin walks away. Beat: open rupture.

chapters.title: The Undertow Manuscript
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she begins reconstructing Ianto's unfinished piece from his notation, discovering it encodes dates and phrases—a diary in music. Beat: grief transmuted into detective work; hope.

chapters.title: Rhys Knows
chapters.summary: Rhys, POV: he confesses he recognized her from the start; his own daughter died estranged from him, and he understands unsaid things. He encourages Emrys to finish the piece. Beat: surrogate fatherhood; permission to grieve.

chapters.title: Nia Confronts the Janitor
chapters.summary: Nia, POV: she plays 'Undertow' fragments she found in the archive—no wait, she plays the phrase she overheard at night—and says, 'You're her.' Emrys neither confirms nor denies, but her hands do. Beat: mask slipping.

chapters.title: Aled's Confession
chapters.summary: Aled, POV: Emrys visits him; he finally admits he saw Ianto walk into the water and froze, believing it a game until too late—and that Merrin helped bury his guilt to protect him. Beat: the family's architecture of silence fully exposed.

chapters.title: Why I Went to the Water
chapters.summary: Ianto, POV (the only chapter in his voice, drawn from the notebook): his final weeks—pressure of being the un-famous sibling, his own quiet despair, and a last message of love, not blame. Beat: devastating tenderness; recontextualizes everything.

chapters.title: Reading It Whole
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she reads the entire letter. Ianto asks her to keep playing, and tells her his drowning was a choice he made alone—absolving her of the guilt she'd carried since she was twelve and missed his call that night. Beat: catharsis and collapse.

chapters.title: The Missed Call
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: full flashback to age twelve—the recital, the voicemail she never played because Merrin confiscated her phone, the morning after. Beat: the novel's buried wound opened; her 'failure' was engineered.

chapters.title: Rage, Then Quiet
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: fury at Merrin—she drives through the night, nearly leaving forever, then stops at the cove. She realizes Merrin burned the note out of terror, not malice. Beat: anger metabolizing into complicated forgiveness.

chapters.title: Merrin Breaks
chapters.summary: Merrin, POV: present day—she finds Emrys waiting on her doorstep. For the first time in ten years, Merrin weeps and tells the whole truth aloud. Beat: the family's central silence finally broken between two people.

chapters.title: Finishing Undertow
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: winter months of reconstruction with Rhys and, secretly, Nia's help with orchestration questions. The final bars resist her until she realizes Ianto left them unfinished on purpose—for whoever came after. Beat: creative resurrection.

chapters.title: The Portrait Comes Down
chapters.summary: Conservatory director, brief POV: budget cuts force the hall's renovation; the portrait of young Emrys is taken down, and staff assume the janitor will be pleased. She isn't and is. Beat: irony; the past officially erased just as she reclaims it.

chapters.title: Application
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she applies to premiere 'Undertow' at the conservatory's spring concert under her real name. The committee debates whether the prodigy's return is stunt or redemption. Beat: stakes raised; public exposure imminent.

chapters.title: Rehearsal in the Empty Hall
chapters.summary: Emrys and Nia, alternating POV: first full run-through. Nia now knows everything and keeps her confidence. Emrys's hands shake through the third movement. Beat: fear and fellowship intertwined.

chapters.title: Merrin in the Back Row
chapters.summary: Merrin, POV: she attends the dress rehearsal uninvited, sitting in darkness. Hearing Ianto's notes in a living room of sound, she finally hears what her silence cost. Beat: mourning given music.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Nia, POV: a local journalist gets wind that the vanished prodigy is premiering a dead brother's work; the story threatens to turn the concert into spectacle. Emrys must decide whether to cancel or claim it. Beat: external crisis at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Claiming the Name
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: she gives one interview, on her terms, correcting the myth of her 'mysterious breakdown'—naming the family silence, not scandal, as the reason she stopped. Beat: agency seized; identity reclaimed publicly.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: sleepless, she visits the cove at midnight, speaks to Ianto at the waterline, and leaves the original letter folded in the piano bench where he used to hide things. Beat: ritual, release, readiness.

chapters.title: Undertow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in short sections—Nia backstage, Merrin in row F, Aled listening on a radio in the harbor office, Rhys in the wings: the performance itself. Emrys plays the finished piece and speaks its dedication aloud. Beat: climax; the almost-said finally said.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the green room afterward—Merrin embraces her without explanation needed; Aled arrives soaked from rain, having driven all night; Nia asks her to mentor her. Beat: belonging rebuilt, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: The House on the Hill
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the developer's demolition begins; Emrys salvages one doorframe and the porch bell. She installs the bell at her new rented cottage above the cove. Beat: carrying the past forward rather than being anchored by it.

chapters.title: Lessons
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: months later, she teaches a small Saturday class of beginners—including a boy who reminds her painfully of Ianto. She teaches them to play wrong notes bravely. Beat: legacy redirected; healing enacted.

chapters.title: An Inventory, Revised
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: closing chapter—she writes her own inventory of what remains: a restored piano, a brother's manuscript published, a mother learning to say things, a name spoken without flinching. Final image: the tide coming in, unhurried. Beat: resolution; memory and belonging reconciled.
